what: Outcome populations with a stated terminal return, adverse excursion and give-up distance per subject. What is authored is the numbers; the rule applied to them is the shipped one.
whatItCannotSay: Nothing about what the real distribution looks like. These say what the bound computes over a population, not what any population is.
whyItIsOwed: The captured night has no closed horizon, so the weekly bound over the fixture is computed from nothing and correctly writes no row. The arithmetic needs populations rather than bars, which is the same reason the cap scenarios are authored.
theUnitsAreTheWholePoint: Each subject states its excursion in ATR and its give-up distance in daily ranges, with the two prices that convert between them. Those are different units on different bases, both small and both looking like volatility, so a comparison made raw produces a bound that reads as perfectly reasonable and is wrong. `stopped-only-in-the-wrong-units` is the case that catches it: read raw its subjects survive, read correctly they do not, and the bound moves from 1.0000 to 0.0000.

scenarios.name: half-the-room-unused
scenarios.why: The shape ARCHITECTURE describes: an achieved rate well under the bound, so better selection has somewhere to go. Four subjects end ahead and two of those survived the path, against eight in the population.

scenarios.name: the-stop-is-the-constraint
scenarios.why: The opposite conclusion from a similar achieved rate. Almost everything that ended ahead was stopped out on the way, so the bound sits barely above what was achieved and no selection change can help. This is the reading that points the loop at the exit rule instead, and telling it apart from the case above is the entire purpose of computing a bound.

scenarios.name: nothing-ended-ahead
scenarios.why: A population where no subject finished in front. The bound is nought and it is a real nought rather than a division by zero: no selection over these rows could have won anything.

scenarios.name: stopped-only-in-the-wrong-units
scenarios.why: The units trap made visible. Every subject has an excursion of -0.9 ATR against a give-up of 0.5 daily ranges, and read as bare numbers 0.9 exceeds 0.5 so nothing survives. Converted properly the excursion is 0.9 in price against a give-up of 5.0, so everything survives and the bound is 1.0000. A ceiling that compared the two multiples raw would report 0.0000 here and be confidently wrong.

scenarios.name: no-range-cannot-be-judged
scenarios.why: A subject with no range at all is treated as not having survived rather than as having survived. A bound that counted unmeasurable rows as available would be optimistic exactly where the data is worst, which is the direction an error must never take.
